lesson_title: Magnetism: The Divorce That Physics Forbids
hook_text: Cut a magnet in half to keep the north end. You can't. Nobody can. Ever. Here's why.
clip_script: Take a magnetised pin — north at the point, south at the head. Snip it in the middle, planning to pocket just the north half. Check your half: it has grown a brand-new south end exactly at the cut. Snip again — same trick. Grind the pin to dust and every speck is a complete two-poled magnet. No laboratory on Earth has ever isolated a lone north or a lone south. Why? Because a magnet was never north-stuff welded to south-stuff. Inside the steel, countless tiny fields have synchronised like a stadium crowd all doing the wave. Cut the stadium in half and both halves are still doing the wave. There was never a north half to keep.
visual_style: Macro shot of scissors snipping a glowing pin, new poles flashing into existence at every cut; zoom into the metal to show domain arrows snapping into a stadium wave.
mood: Playful defiance — an impossible challenge the viewer keeps losing.
pacing: Quick snip-snip-snip escalation, beat of disbelief, slow-motion zoom into the domain crowd, punchline landing on the wave.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson to draw the invisible field — and meet the magnet you're standing on.
